auth.quote: The V2 API requires an access token to authenticate requests.
The API can be accessed by creating a Personal Access Token from the Developers section of Harvest ID.
If you are interested in building integrations that other users can use, you will need to register an OAuth2 Application, also known as an OAuth2 Client.
Personal Access Tokens replace the Basic Authentication method that was used in our v1 API, as this is more secure.

notes: OAuth2 apps (authorization code for server-side, plus implicit for client-side) are self-registered in Harvest ID's Developers section with no documented app review. The API can also be called with a PAT (Bearer header or access_token query param plus a Harvest-Account-Id header). A User-Agent header with app name and contact is required. The API is broad: about 50 resource pages (clients, contacts, invoices, estimates, expenses, tasks, time entries, projects, assignments, roles, users, rates, reports, PTO, approvals, notifications, reimbursements, imports, Gusto integration and Forecast endpoints), well over 50 operations. Rate limits are 100 requests per 15 seconds generally and 100 per 15 minutes for the Reports API. The official remote MCP (api.harvestapp.com/mcp, OAuth via id.getharvest.com) covers timers, time entries, reports, budgets, projects, clients, tasks, assignments, draft invoices, expenses and timesheet approval submission. Many community Harvest MCP servers also exist on GitHub (taiste, ianaleck, southleft, etc.). The harvesthq GitHub org has no MCP repo.
